_: Copy this to launch.config.json and fill in every CHANGE ME. That file is gitignored and stays on the machine that launches: the salt decides the token address, so a salt in a public repository is a token address anyone can take.
name: VITALS
_expectedEconomics: The factory's commitment to the economics of this config and pair. Read off a recent successful ETH-pair launch on config 0 and verified live before every send: if the factory's economics change, the launch refuses rather than going out on terms nobody agreed to. bytes32(0) would disable the check; it is deliberately not used.
_salt: Decides the token address, together with the sender and the params. 32 bytes, yours, never committed. --check prints the address this salt produces, so the CA is known before the transaction.
_devBuyEth: The opening buy. Refused above 5% of supply. At our 4% creator tax 0.0930 ETH takes 4.9962% and 0.0931 takes 5.0012%, which the cap refuses: the safe four-decimal value is 0.0930. See the table in docs/launch-configs.md.
_extraExemptions: Wallets exempt from the opening tax BESIDES the deployer, which the tool adds itself. Empty is the declared position: nobody gets in tax free but the wallet that launched it.

rehearsal._: The rehearsal launches a real token on the real chain, so it never carries the production ticker: a second VITALS on chain before launch is the thing the collision check exists to catch.

_recipients: creatorFeeRecipient takes the creator tax, recipient takes the opening buy. Both are the deployer wallet for our launch. --check refuses any other address.
